item.title: Permanent or Professional? The Three Kinds of Knot | Hilchot Shabbat | Siman 317:1
item.description:
When is a knot forbidden on Shabbat? The three kinds of knot in Siman 317:1: the Mishnah's camel drivers and sailors, the Gemara's reconciliation of three baraitot, and the hilazon fishers' nets in the Mishkan, with the Radbaz taking it literally.

item.title: How Long Can a Knot Stay Tied? 24 Hours, 7 Days or More | Hilchot Shabbat | Siman 317:1
item.description:
How long can a knot last before it becomes forbidden on Shabbat? Siman 317:1: a Torah prohibition needs a permanent, professional knot, with lesser knots rabbinic or permitted. The class sets out how the Mishnah Berurah, the Shulhan Arukh HaRav, Rashi and the Rosh define the middle category.

item.title: Shoelaces, Headscarves & Sefer Torah Bands: Knots in Practice | Hilchot Shabbat | Siman 317:5
item.description:

item.title: Should Women Say Shehiyanu at Candle Lighting? | Hilchot Shabbat | Siman 263:5
item.description:
Is Shehiyanu said when lighting candles? Siman 263:5: the berakhah is lehadlik ner shel Shabbat, same for men and women, and on Yom Tov lehadlik ner shel Yom Tov. The Mishnah Berurah says a woman should not say Shehiyanu at the lighting because it comes at Kiddush.

item.title: Does Lighting Candles Mean Accepting Shabbat? | Hilchot Shabbat | Siman 263:10-12
item.description:
Siman 263 asks whether lighting Shabbat candles itself means accepting Shabbat. The class sets the Bahag's view against the Rosh, Tosafot, Ramban and Rashba, who rely on the Gemara's three blasts, then covers stipulating, the match custom, and how the Shulhan Arukh's second opinion rules.

item.title: Mosquitoes, Toothpaste & Lemons: Killing and Squeezing on Shabbat | Hilchot Shabbat
item.description:
May you swat a mosquito or squeeze a lemon on Shabbat? The class covers trapping and killing insects, spraying, flushing a toilet over insects, with five reasons to permit, and squeezing fruit. The Shulhan Arukh forbids trapping a flea unless it is biting, and never killing it.
